# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

(empty)

Turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — so this round, my gesture lands on Deaf (since Deaf comes after me). Deaf can then speak next round... wait, actually speaking order is fixed per round: Mute, Blind, Deaf. Blind goes before Deaf, so Blind won't hear Deaf until next round. That's fine, we have multiple rounds.

I need to establish a gesture code for colors and order. Let me use simple distinct symbols for purple, blue, red, and convey "cut in this order: purple, blue, red."

Let me assign: ☝ = first, ✌ = second, 🤟 = third (numbers), and colors: 🫱=purple, 🫲=blue, 🫳=red. I'll send this mapping plus the sequence, but Deaf has no way to know my mapping means anything unless I explain — but I can't speak, only gesture, and Deaf can see gestures fine. I need to define the code implicitly by repetition/structure since I can't attach text labels. Best approach: send gestures in the order matching the manual sequence, and let Deaf match them against what they see on the bomb (colors in some order/position). Since Deaf sees actual colors, I should just signal order using numbers paired with... but I don't know Deaf's view yet (colors/markings), and Deaf hasn't sent anything yet.

Best first move: wait, since I have no info about what Deaf sees, and gesturing blind (pun intended) risks wrong mapping. Actually I should send my instructions in a self-defining way: use color-coded gestures that are common/intuitive isn't possible since gestures are hand symbols, not colors. I'll invent a numbered sequence code and wait for Deaf to describe the bomb's wire colors first via... but Deaf can't send to me, only I send to Deaf. Deaf's speech goes to Blind only (I can't hear).

So actually the only channel I have is gesture to Deaf. Deaf must interpret my gestures as instructions and relay via speech to Blind. I should just pick a fixed order-encoding: gesture three symbols representing "purple, blue, red" using distinct symbols, then Deaf needs a way to know which symbol = which color. Since I can't label them, I'll rely on Deaf to figure out via elimination: I'll send exactly 3 distinct gestures, implying "cut wires in this order, and I'll clarify which is which next round once you tell me colors." But I can't receive anything from Deaf.

Simplest robust protocol: send gestures for colors using intuitive symbol-color associations that might be culturally guessed, but that's unreliable. Better: send count/order info only, and trust Deaf to see purple, blue, red are the actual bomb colors matching my manual - Deaf reads gestures as ordinal positions referencing colors Deaf already sees. I'll gesture using distinct symbols to represent purple=1st, blue=2nd, red=3rd, using number-like gestures: ☝ (one), ✌ (two), 🤟 (three) to indicate order, then separately gesture for colors is impossible without a shared code.

Given constraints, I'll establish the code myself now and trust it's the only sensible interpretation given Deaf will see wire colors and can match by elimination if only 3 wires exist matching purple/blue/red.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫱", "☝", "🫲", "✌", "🫳", "🤟"])
```

then the red wire.

Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I feel a keypad with four keys showing digits one five two eight in that order. It shows one digit slot entered and nothing entered yet. I feel a strip with three raised marks but cannot tell what they mean. I feel six wires but not their colors. I need to know from the manual what order to press keys, which wire to cut, or what the strip means. Please relay instructions.

This is very informative. My manual says: "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the red wire." Deaf reports wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. So purple is wire 5, blue is wire 3, red is wire 4.

I need to tell Blind the correct cutting order (wire 5, then wire 3, then wire 4) via gestures to Deaf, who will then speak it to Blind. I cannot speak or send text — only gestures to Deaf. I need a numeric gesture code Deaf can translate to Blind via speech.

I'll use finger-count gestures for numbers: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4(or use 4-finger symbol)... Let's define clearly: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5 (open hand often signifies 5), ✋=4... Actually let's keep it simple and use a unary/count system Deaf can obviously map: I'll send groups of ☝ repeated to indicate numbers, separated by a pause symbol like 👋 to mark boundaries.

Plan: send "cut order = 5, 3, 4" as counts of ☝ separated by 👋.

Sequence: ☝☝☝☝☝ (5 ones) 👋 ☝☝☝ (3 ones) 👋 ☝☝☝☝ (4 ones)

This is unambiguous to count.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👋","☝","☝","☝","👋","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

The wire info is unchanged, confirming purple=5, blue=3, red=4. I already sent the gesture code (5,3,4 counts of ☝ separated by 👋) to Deaf last turn. I should wait to see if Deaf successfully translates and speaks it to Blind, since Blind only hears speech from Deaf in the round after Deaf speaks (turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf — Deaf's speech this round would reach Blind next round).

Nothing new to send since my instruction stands; I'll wait unless I want to reinforce. Let me just wait this turn to see Deaf's next update and confirm the relay worked.

Deaf says to Mute: Light just turned green for the first time, display shows 3. I see your pattern of five, three, four repeated. Waiting for confirmation this is the trigger.

Deaf correctly decoded my gesture pattern as five, three, four. Now Deaf needs to speak this to Blind as the wire-cutting order. Send: 🤏 (wire) followed by sequence 5,3,4 (as counts of ☝ separated by 👋), then 👍 confirm, meaning "wire sequence: 5,3,4, confirmed - relay to Blind as cut wire 5 then wire 3 then wire 4."
